prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” roofing company that fits every situation — the right contractor depends on your location in Dallas, the roof type, your budget, whether you’re making an insurance claim, and the timeline. I can help you find the best option for your needs. Meanwhile, here are practical steps and red flags to quickly identify a high-quality roofer in Dallas:

How to find a top roofer
- Get at least 3 written estimates that break out materials, labor, tear-off vs. overlay, permit costs, disposal, and timeline.
- Search local reviews: Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi, Nextdoor. Look for consistent recent positive reviews and prompt replies to complaints.
- Check credentials: Dallas/COLLEGE? Some Texas cities require contractor registration — check City of Dallas permitting/inspection records for active registration and open permits. Ask for proof of insurance (general liability and worker’s comp).
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc. Certified contractors can offer extended warranties.
- Ask for references and recent local jobs you can inspect.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed/registered with the City of Dallas (if applicable)? Can you provide permit numbers for past projects?
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can I see certificates of insurance?
- Who will supervise the job and who is the point of contact?
- Will you obtain permits and handle inspections?
- What exactly is included in the estimate? (materials, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, drip edge, disposal)
- What warranties do you provide (manufacturer vs. workmanship) and are they written?
- Do you provide lien waivers and final paperwork?

What to expect in a good contract
- Start and completion dates, payment schedule (avoid large up-front payments), full scope of work, list of materials and colors, disposal and cleanup plan, permit responsibility, warranty terms, and lien release upon final payment.

Red flags
- High-pressure sales tactics or demand for large up-front cash payments.
- No insurance certificates or reluctance to provide references.
- Vague estimates (no details on materials or labor).
- Too-good-to-be-true low prices.
- No written contract or refusal to pull permits.

Resources to check
- Google Maps reviews / Yelp
- Better Business Bureau (BBB.org)
- Angi / HomeAdvisor
- City of Dallas permitting/inspections website
- Manufacturer locator pages (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) for certified contractors

If you’d like, tell me:
- your zip code or neighborhood,
- whether this is residential or commercial,
- roof material (asphalt shingles, tile, metal) and approximate roof size/age,
- are you filing an insurance claim?

I can then pull a short, vetted list of local roofers and help you compare their quotes.
